title: Burning with Curiosity
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Alice's Adventures in Wonderland by Lewis Carroll (1865).
body: Alice was beginning to get very tired of sitting by her sister on the bank, and of having nothing to do: once or twice she had peeped into the book her sister was reading, but it had no pictures or conversations in it, "and what is the use of a book," thought Alice "without pictures or conversations?"

So she was considering in her own mind (as well as she could, for the hot day made her feel very sleepy and stupid), whether the pleasure of making a daisy-chain would be worth the trouble of getting up and picking the daisies, when suddenly a White Rabbit with pink eyes ran close by her. There was nothing so very remarkable in that; nor did Alice think it so very much out of the way to hear the Rabbit say to itself, "Oh dear! Oh dear! I shall be late!" but when the Rabbit actually took a watch out of its waistcoat-pocket, and looked at it, and then hurried on, Alice started to her feet, for it flashed across her mind that she had never before seen a rabbit with either a waistcoat-pocket, or a watch to take out of it, and burning with curiosity, she ran across the field after it, and fortunately was just in time to see it pop down a large rabbit-hole under the hedge.

In another moment down went Alice after it, never once considering how in the world she was to get out again. The rabbit-hole went straight on like a tunnel for some way, and then dipped suddenly down, so suddenly that Alice had not a moment to think about stopping herself before she found herself falling down a very deep well.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why was Alice tired?
options: Of sitting by her sister and having nothing to do
Of running through the field all afternoon
Of reading a very long book by herself
Of arguing with her sister about a rabbit

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did Alice think was missing from her sister's book?
options: Pictures or conversations
A title page
An interesting plot
Illustrations of rabbits

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what kind of animal ran close by Alice?
options: A White Rabbit with pink eyes
A gray cat with green eyes
A brown dog with a collar
A black bird with a red beak

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did the Rabbit say to itself?
options: "Oh dear! Oh dear! I shall be late!"
"Curiouser and curiouser!"
"Off with her head!"
"We're all mad here!"

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Rabbit take out of its waistcoat-pocket?
options: A watch
A key
A letter
A pair of gloves

questions.prompt: Per the passage, where did Alice see the Rabbit pop down?
options: A large rabbit-hole under the hedge
A hole beneath a tree
A door in the garden wall
A well beside the bank

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why did Alice jump to her feet and chase after the Rabbit?
options: She had never before seen a rabbit with a waistcoat-pocket or a watch, and it startled her curiosity
She wanted to return the watch to its rightful owner
Her sister told her to follow the Rabbit
She was frightened and wanted to escape from it

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the narrator mention that the hot day made Alice feel "sleepy and stupid" just before the Rabbit appears?
options: To show she was drowsy and inattentive, making the Rabbit's sudden, odd appearance feel all the more striking
To explain why Alice fell asleep and dreamed the entire story
To suggest that Alice was too tired to notice the Rabbit at all
To show that the weather had made Alice ill

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the overall point of the passage?
options: Alice, bored and drowsy, is drawn into a strange adventure when curiosity leads her to chase an oddly human rabbit down a hole
Alice spends the whole passage happily reading a picture book with her sister
Alice is frightened by a rabbit and runs home to safety
Alice deliberately digs a hole to search for a lost watch

questions.prompt: As used in the passage, what does it mean that there was "nothing so very remarkable" in the Rabbit running by?
options: Nothing especially unusual or worth noticing
Nothing that could be seen clearly
Nothing that made a sound
Nothing that was dangerous

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what was Alice considering before the Rabbit appeared?
options: Whether making a daisy-chain was worth the trouble of getting up
Whether to go swimming in a nearby pond
Whether to ask her sister for a different book
Whether to take a nap on the bank

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what shape did the rabbit-hole take at first?
options: Straight, like a tunnel
Round, like a bowl
Twisted, like a spiral staircase
Narrow, like a chimney

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happened to the tunnel after it went straight for a while?
options: It dipped suddenly down
It came to a dead end
It split into two paths
It grew narrower and narrower

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did Alice find herself falling down after the tunnel dipped?
options: A very deep well
A steep, rocky cliff
A grassy hillside
A flight of stone stairs

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why didn't Alice think it "very much out of the way" to hear the Rabbit talk to itself?
options: In the drowsy, dreamlike moment, the strangeness of it didn't strike her until she thought it over afterward
She had heard the same rabbit speak on many earlier occasions
She assumed her sister had trained the rabbit to talk
She could not actually hear what the Rabbit was saying

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what leads Alice down the rabbit hole?
options: Her curiosity about the unusual Rabbit overcomes her drowsy boredom, and she follows it without thinking of the consequences
She is chasing the Rabbit to retrieve a watch it stole from her sister
She falls into the hole by accident while picking daisies
Her sister pushes her into the hole as a joke

questions.prompt: As used in the passage, what does it mean that Alice was "burning with curiosity"?
options: Feeling an intense eagerness to find out something
Feeling physically overheated from the sun
Feeling angry about being ignored
Feeling too tired to move any further
